motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend Council:

WHEREAS rural villages across Ottawa have experienced a decline in local services, including banks, retail stores, and other essential commercial uses that support complete and vibrant communities; and
WHEREAS rural residents, landowners, and businesses have identified a need for planning policies, zoning standards, and approval processes that better reflect rural realities, including the distinct needs of farms, village main streets, rural businesses, and unserviced properties; and
WHEREAS many rural properties on mainstreets and in commercial corridors consist of unserviced or legacy-sized lots that face development constraints thatmay limit the ability of landowners, entrepreneurs, and businesses to repurpose or reinvest in rural properties for viable commercial uses; and
WHEREAS advancements in private servicing, site design, and low-impact development may provide opportunities to safely and effectively use smaller or unserviced lots, while supporting rural economic revitalization; and
WHEREAS feedback received through the City’s 2024 Rural Summit identified key issues affecting rural economic development suggesting that current zoning, planning policies, and approval processes should be reviewed to identify whether they unintentionally create barriers to investment, business development, and economic diversification in rural villages, and to support rural growth that is practical, context-sensitive, and respectful of rural character.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff within Planning, Development and Building Services staff report back to the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee with:
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff recommend additional improvements drawing from insights about barriers to rural economic growth from their experience supporting rural entrepreneurs through the development review process to date, as well as through consultations with rural stakeholders, including business owners, landowners and agricultural representatives to further identify barriers and opportunities; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that provide an update on the progress of this work to the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee by the end of Q3 2026.

WHEREAS the City of Ottawa’s rural villages, including the Village of Carp, serve as important economic, cultural, and social hubs that support local businesses, tourism, and community identity; and
WHEREAS retail and service businesses form the backbone of rural village economies and rely on accessible infrastructure, including adequate parking, to attract customers, support employment, and sustain local economic activity; and
WHEREAS consultation undertaken through the 2024 Ottawa Rural Summit and the Rural Economic Development Plan identified infrastructure, transportation, and parking capacity in village cores as key constraints to economic growth and barriers to business viability; and
WHEREAS stakeholders specifically identified the need for additional municipal parking and improved visitor infrastructure in rural villages to support tourism, local spending, and business success; and
WHEREAS the Rural Economic Development Plan emphasizes the importance of integrating rural economic considerations into City decision-making, including infrastructure investments such as transportation and parking that support and strengthen the rural economy; and
WHEREAS the Plan also identifies the importance of coordinated, place-based economic development and investments in village infrastructure to sustain and grow rural economies; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa Official Plan directs growth to rural villages as focal points for economic activity, service delivery, and community life, and supports investments in public realm and infrastructure that enhance the viability and attractiveness of these areas; and
WHEREAS improving access to businesses in village cores aligns with Council’s priorities to support a diversified and prosperous economy and to strengthen rural economic resilience;
THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED THAT:

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approve the recommendations on the Rural Community-Building Grants Program applications as detailed in this report and Document 1.

BE IT RESOLVED that this Motion with respect to the revised grant submission from the Metcalfe Farmers Market be considered at today's meeting pursuant to subsection 89(3) of the Procedure By-law so that it may be considered alongside the Rural Community Building Grant Program report already on the agenda.
WHEREAS the Metcalfe Farmers’ Market applied to the City of Ottawa’s Rural Community Building Grant Program for a permanent sign to commemorate the 33rdyear of the market, a shade tent and some event signs; and
WHEREAS on April 2, 2026, Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approved report ACS2026-PDB-PS-0030, which included an application for the Metcalfe Farmers’ Market under the Rural Community Building Grant Program; and
WHEREAS the Metcalfe Farmers’ Market has requested to adjust their grant to exchange the permanent sign for a projector to show images and graphics on the back wall of the market, allowing more flexibility and the ability to keep updating the imagery; and
WHEREAS the Metcalfe Farmers’ Market will not exceed the already existing and allocated budget.
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee approve the request of the Metcalfe Farmers’ Market to substitute a projector, instead of the permanent commemorative sign that is outlined in report ACS2026-PDB-PS-0030.

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee (ARAC) meeting of Thursday, 2 April 2026, Councillor I. Skalski introduced the Motion (below) as a Notice of Motion, to be considered at the Committee’s next meeting.
Prior to the delivery of the ARAC meeting agenda of 7 May 2026, Councillor Skalski revised her original Motion as provided further below, further to which it was again revised pursuant to Subsection 59(5) of the Procedure By-law to introduce amended wording, underlined for ease of reference.
The Committee then heard from Aaron Kelly, Community Associations for Environmental Sustainability (CAFES), who spoke to a prepared slide presentation to illustrate his points.  A copy of his presentation is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.  Written correspondence was also received from Roddy Bolivar, Executive Director, Carp Road BIA Board of Management.  A copy of his submission is also held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
At the conclusion of Committee discussions, the updated ARAC Motion NO 2026 35-06 was put before Committee and was ‘Carried’, as amended at the meeting of 7 May 2026, as outlined below.

motions.motion_text:
Notice of Motion (as introduced at ARAC on 02 April 2026):
WHEREAS rural residents in the City of Ottawa rely on private infrastructure including drilled wells, septic systems, and permanent standby power systems to safely occupy their homes; and
WHEREAS having running water and functioning sanitary systems is an essential upgrade that can put unexpected pressure on family budgets; and
WHEREAS climate change is increasing pressure on private water and wastewater systems, including more frequent and severe drought conditions, extreme rainfall events, and power outages that directly affect rural households; and
WHEREAS this year’s exceptional drought conditions have highlighted the vulnerability of private wells and the growing need for resilient water infrastructure in rural communities; and
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa already operates the Better Homes Ottawa program, which provides financing to homeowners through a Local Improvement Charge model that allows upgrades to be repaid over time through the property tax bill; and
WHEREAS this financing structure has proven to be an effective tool for enabling homeowners to make major investments that improve environmental sustainability and climate resilience; and
WHEREAS the Better Homes Ottawa Loan Program is scheduled to undergo a comprehensive program review, including alignment with Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) partnership requirements; and
WHEREAS there is currently no comparable financing program available to rural residents to support essential infrastructure upgrades such as wells, septic systems, and permanently installed standby generators;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that City Council direct staff to include, as part of the upcoming Better Homes Ottawa program review, an assessment of opportunities to expand or adapt the program to support rural infrastructure upgrades, including private wells, septic systems, and permanently installed standby generators; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff be directed to evaluate the feasibility of delivering such a program through:
AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that the staff report include:
options for financing using a Local Improvement Charge or similar property-based repayment model; potential funding sources, including federal and provincial climate-adaptation and resilience programs; eligibility criteria that prioritize climate resilience, water security, and protection of groundwater resources; and a proposed implementation timeline and estimated financial impact to the City;
AND BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff report back to the appropriate Standing Committee and Council as part of the Better Homes Ottawa Loan Program review, anticipated in Q3 2027.

sub_agendas_items.title: Motion - Councillor C. Kitts – Improving Road Safety at Tenth Line Road and Wall Road

attachments.attachment_title: Motion - ACS2026-OCC-CCS-0054 - C Kitts - Improving Road Safety.pdf

sub_agendas_items.minutes:
At the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee (ARAC) meeting of Thursday, 2 April 2026, Councillor I. Skalski introduced the following as a Notice of Motion on behalf of Councillor C. Kitts, to be considered at the ARAC meeting of 7 May 2026.
ARAC Motion NO 2026 35-07 was put before Committee and was ‘Carried’, as presented.

motions.motion_text:
Motion
That the Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee recommend Council:

WHEREAS the intersection of Tenth Line Road and Wall Road is a rural intersection experiencing increased traffic volumes due to ongoing growth and development in the area; and
WHEREAS recent collision data provided by the Ottawa Police Service indicates an emerging trend, with six reported collisions in 2024 and 2025 combined and highlights the importance of ongoing efforts to support driver awareness and road safety; and
WHEREAS the intersection meets the City’s traffic signal warrant criteria and a permanent solution, such as traffic signals or a roundabout, is anticipated to be considered through the 2027 budget process and any interim measures would be subject to staff review, prioritization, and available funding; and
WHEREAS the City is implementing interim safety improvements at this location, including enhanced warning signage, larger stop signs, pavement marking changes, and lighting adjustments; and
WHEREAS the intersection does not currently meet City’s requirements or provincial recommendations for the installation of flashing mounted beacons; and
WHEREAS flashing warning beacons mounted on signs are a relatively low-cost intervention that can improve driver awareness and reduce the risk of angle and high-speed collisions at rural intersections;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to install mounted flashing warning beacons on signs at the intersection of Tenth Line Road and Wall Road as an interim safety measure; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that funding for this work be allocated from the existing general Traffic Services Operations budget; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that staff continue to monitor collision data at this intersection and report back as part of future budget considerations for a permanent intersection control solution, in consultation with the Ward Councillor.

sub_agendas_items.title: Replacement of Septic System Infrastructure at 2761 8th Line Road (Stanley Apartments) - Village of Metcalfe
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Councillor I. Skalski introduced the following Motion pertaining to the Replacement of Septic System Infrastructure at 2761 8th Line Road (Stanley Apartments) in the Village of Metcalfe, asked that Committee waive the Rules of Procedure to deal with it due to the time-sensitivity of the matter, and she spoke to the Motion to provide context.
Motion NO ARAC 2026 35-09 was then put before Committee, and its recommendations were ‘Carried’, as presented.

motions.motion_text:
That the Rules of Procedure be suspended to consider the following motion at today’s meeting as the matter is time sensitive as the septic system infrastructure at 2761 8thLine Road is in distress and requires replacement.
WHEREAS the Stanley Apartments at 2761 8thLine Road in the Village of Metcalfe are operated by a not-for-profit corporation; and
WHEREAS the apartment complex needs a new septic system to be installed, which due to its size requires Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) from the province; and
WHEREAS there is sign off on the application form that is required from the City to establish the municipality's general concurrence with the proposal and to ensure that the proposed works would not contravene any municipal by-laws or other requirements; and
WHEREAS the project does not require any type of planning approvals by the City, meaning that Planning, Development and Building Services staff do not have delegated authority to sign off on the ECA application to the Ministry;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that once Planning Services staff have been provided with the full application package and deemed it to be satisfactory, that Council delegate authority to the Director of Infrastructure and Water Services to sign off on the ECA application form required to be submitted to the Ministry.
